The petitioners have filed this petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1989, claiming the compensation of Rs.60,00,000/- from the respondents with regard to the death of M. Nagendra in the road traffic accident that took place on 04.04.2023.

2. The brief facts of the case of the petitioners as follows:
On 04.04.2023 at 12.50 p.m. when the deceased was driving the TATA Intra Goods Tempo bearing Reg. No.AP-39-UL-9821, near Sri Lakshmi Prasanna Nursery Garden, near Panthanahalli Village, on Kuppam-V.Kota Road, K.G.F. Taluk, Kolar District, at that time, the driver of the Lorry bearing Reg. No.TN-52-J-2262 came from opposite direction i.e., from V. Kota side with high speed and in a rash and negligent manner.
As a result, the driver of the Lorry lost control over his vehicle and the said lorry went to its wrong side of the road and dashed against the deceased's Goods Tempo.
Due to impact, the deceased sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the said injuries on the spot.

It is further contended that, immediately after the accident, the dead body was shifted to General Hospital, Robertsonpet,
K.G.F wherein post-mortem was conducted and the dead body was handed over to the petitioners and they have performed the last rites and obsequies of the deceased by spending huge amount towards medical and funeral expenses.
3. It is stated that the deceased was aged about 30 years and was working as driver cum owner of Goods Tempo and earning Rs.50,000/- per month.
The deceased was the only bread earner of their family and due to his death, the petitioners are undergoing mental shock and agony and facing great financial difficulties.
It is further stated that the accident in question was due to the rash and negligence on the part of the driver of the offending Lorry bearing Reg. No. TN-52-J-2262.

Hence,
the 1 st respondent being the owner and 2nd respondent being the Insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners.
4. Inspite of service of summons, the 1 st respondent remained exparte.
On service of notice, 2nd respondent appeared before the court through its counsel and filed written statement.
5. The 2nd Respondent in its objections has stated that the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts and hence the petition is liable to be dismissed.
It has denied the age, income and occupation of the deceased.
It has also denied the amount spent towards the funeral expenses of the deceased.

This respondent has admitted the issuance Policy in favour of respondent No.1 in respect of the offending Lorry bearing Reg. No.TN-52-J-2262 and the liability if any is subject to the terms and conditions of the policy, provision of MV Act, valid and effective driving licence held by the driver of the Lorry, valid RC, permit and FC and also subject to the confirmation of Sec.64 VB of the insurance Act.
Respondent also seeks protection under section 147 and 149 of M.V. Act.
It has also contended that owner and jurisdictional police have not complied the Sec.134(c) and Sec.158(6) of M.V. Act.
It has denied the alleged negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle.
Further contended that the compensation and interest claimed by the petitioners are excessive and exorbitant.
Hence on all these grounds, it has sought for dismissal of the petition.

3 6. Based on the pleadings, this court has framed following issues:-
ISSUES 1. Whether the petitioners prove that the deceased Sri M. Nagendra has died in the road traffic accident occurred on 04.04.2023 at about 12.50 p.m. near Sri Lakshmi Prasanna Nursery Garden, Panthanahalli Village, on Kuppam-V.Kota road, K.G.F Taluk, Kolar District, due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Lorry bearing Reg. No.TN-52-J-2262?
2.
Whether the petitioners are entitled for any compensation?

If so, to what extent and from whom?
3. What order or Award?
7. In order to prove the case, 1 st petitioner got examined herself as PW.1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P1 to 15 documents.
On the other hand, respondent No.2 has examined a witness as RW.1 and got marked the documents at Ex.R1 and Ex.R2.

8. Heard the arguments.
9.

My findings on the above issues as under:-
 Issue No.1 ...

In the partly affirmative,
 Issue No.2 ...

Partly in the affirmative,
 Issue No.4 ...

As per final order  For the following:
 REASONS 10. ISSUE NO.1 : It is the case of the petitioners that, on 04.04.2023 at 12.50 p.m. when the deceased was proceeding in his TATA Intra Goods Tempo bearing Reg. No.AP-39-UL-9821, near Sri Lakshmi Prasanna Nursery Garden, near Panthanahalli Village, on Kuppam-V.Kota Road, K.G.F.
Taluk, Kolar District, at that time, the driver of the Lorry bearing Reg. No.TN-52-J-2262 came from opposite direction i.e., from V. Kota side with high speed and in a rash and negligent manner.
As a result, the driver of the Lorry lost control over his vehicle and the said lorry went to its wrong side of the road and dashed against the deceased's Goods Tempo.
Due to impact, the deceased sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the said injuries on the spot.

It is specifically urged that, the accident happened because of the rash and negligent act of the driver of Lorry and as such the respondents are liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
11.

In order to substantiate the contentions of the petitioners, the petitioner No.1 stepped into the witness box and filed her affidavit-in-lieu of oral examination-in-chief as PW1 and got marked F.I.R,
F.I.S, spot mahazar, sketch, IMV report, Inquest report, P.M. report and charge sheet as per Ex.P1 to Nandini.M vs Sellappa Gounder.

4 Ex.P8.
12.

On the other hand, respondent No.2 has contended that the alleged accident was occurred due to the negligence of deceased himself who was driving the Goods tempo after consuming alcohol and drove it in a rash and negligent manner and dashed the right side of the Lorry in the middle of the road.

In the charge sheet mentioned that, FSL Report says that the deceased had consumed quantum of alcohol at 48.1mg/100ml of blood in Article No.1 and Quantum of Ethyl alcohol 47.6mg/100ml of blood in Article No.2, and at the time of accident he was driving the vehicle without DL.

In order to prove the same, respondent No.2 has examined its Assistant Manager-Legal as RW.1 and got marked the documents at Ex.R1 and Ex.R2 and also relied on the police documents.
13.
This issue revolves round the sphere and ambit as to the alleged rash and negligence on the part of the driver offending vehicle.
The factum of negligence has to be proved like any other fact in issue.
Before dwelling into analyzing the factum of alleged negligence, it is relevant to have the conceptual aspects pertaining to factum of negligence.
There are four basic elements that a person has to fulfill in order to do a negligent act.
These elements are as follows:
Duty: For committing a negligent act, there must be some duty on the part of the defendant.
Here it is important to understand whether the defendant has taken legal duty of care towards the plaintiff.
Breach of Duty:
After fulfilling the first criteria the plaintiff must prove that the defendant has breached the legal duty imposed on him/her.
It talks about the breach of duty on the part of the defendant which he/ she is expected to do as he/ she has some legal duty towards the plaintiff.
The action of causing something: It means that the damage caused to the plaintiff is due to the act of the defendant.
Here the defendant may do an act which is not expected from him/her or the defendant may be negligent in not doing an act which was expected from him/ her.
Damages: At last what matters is, there must be some damage/injury that is caused to the plaintiff and this damages should be the direct consequence of the defendant's act.

Negligence means a breach of duty caused by omission to do something which has reasonable man guide by those consideration which ordinarily regulated conduct of human affairs would do which a prudent man would not do.
In common prevalence negligence connoted to the want of proper care and the rashness conveys the idea of recklessness or the doing of an act without due consideration.
14. I have perused documentary evidence coupled with oral evidence in detail.

As per Ex.P1- FIR filed at Cr.No.0040/2023 of Bethamangala police station clearly shows that on 03.04.2023 and 04.04.2023 mid night at about 12:50 to 1.00 a.m. there was an accident and in the said accident,

5 deceased was the driver of the Tata Intra goods tempo bearing Reg No. AP-39-UL-9821 and he died on the spot.

One Sri Srinivasalu M. has put the law into motion by filing first information and accordingly, Ex.P.1 FIR is registered against the driver of offending vehicle for the offence punishable U/s. 279 and 304(A) of IPC and Sec 134(a and b) of MV Act.
Whereas documents at Ex.P-1 to 5 and 8 i.e. FIR, Complaint, Spot panchanama, Sketch prepared at the time of spot mahazer, IMV report and Charge sheet.

15. It is the contention of the respondent No.2 that, the deceased was under the influence of alcohol at the time of accident and also in PM report it is mentioned that the blood in EDTA is sent to FSL for alcohol percentage estimation as requested by investigating officer and has argued that the accident has taken place due to the rash and negligent act of deceased as he has driven the goods vehicle under the influence of alcohol.
16.

The Charge sheet produced by the petitioners at Ex.P8 clearly discloses that the charge sheet is filed against the driver of the offending vehicle Lorry for rash and negligent driving under IPC 1860 U/s. 279, 304(A) and under Sec 134(a and b) of MV Act.
Further the I.O. also in the charge sheet has mentioned about the said fact of consumption of alcohol as per PM and FSL report to an extent of 47.6mg out of 100 ml blood is containing ethyl alcohol.

17. Whereas the petitioner counsel has argued that even though as per PM and chargesheet there is mention of consumption of alcohol by the deceased, but the accident has taken place on 03.04.2023 midnight at 1.00 a.m. and PM report is conducted on 04.04.2023 between 11.30 a.m. to 12.30 p.m.
for which the PM report and without support of FSL report and only mentioning in the chargesheet cannot be considered and further the said consumption of alcohol itself cannot be a ground to hold that the accident has taken place solely due to the rash and negligent act of deceased.
18.

I would like to rely upon the decision rendered by Hon'ble Madras High Court in C.Misc. Appeal No.1842/2006 in K.Shanmugam vs. V.Krishnamurthy & Another, wherein it is held that the involvement of claimant in the accident due to the fact that he was in drunken stage and also alcohol consumption impairs consciousness and vision which becomes impossible to judge accurately how far the objects are whether it is night or day it can reduce the visibility of an object to the point of being below the limit of discernibility and punishment should be at-least a deterrent for other such persons getting away with minor punishment and fine.
Further, section 185 of M.V. Act to be considered as zero tolerance wherein too many lives have already been lost to this lithel cocktail of internal consumption and combustion.

I.O has mentioned in chargesheet as per FSL report along with PM report which is showing 47.06 mg./100 ml. consumption of alcohol is itself is sufficient to come to conclusion that the deceased was under the influence of alcohol at the time of accident and such being the fact, the consumption of the alcohol is to be considered relying upon the said reports as the drink and drive has become menace to our society due to which several lives are lost and such act of drink and drive by consuming the alcohol has to be considered seriously and hence considering the charge sheet filed by the I.O. showing the deceased was under the influence of alcohol for which some part of contributory negligence for happening of the accident by the deceased if considered will meet the ends of justice.

Also as per sketch and spot mahazer clears that accident occurred in the middle of the road, if the both vehicle drivers were driven the vehicles in Nandini.M vs Sellappa Gounder.P on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/108054948/
6 normal speed, they could have certainly avoided the accident, but no one has taken precautions.

19. Hence, in view of my discussion made earlier it goes to show that, the said accident has taken place due to the contributory negligence by the driver of Lorry and also due to the rash and negligent act of the driver of Tata Intra goods vehicle/deceased.

20. Therefore, in this issue it clearly goes to show that, accident has taken place due to the rash and negligence of both the vehicles attributing to contributory negligence for which the driver of the Tata Intra goods vehicle bearing Reg. No.AP-39-UL- 9821/deceased is saddled @ 20% and driver of the offending Lorry bearing Reg. No.TN/52-J-2262 is saddled with 80% contributory negligence for the cause of accident.
Accordingly I answer Issue No.1 Partly in the Affirmative.
21. ISSUE No.2:
While answering issue No.1, I have already observed that accident has taken place due to the rash and negligence of both the vehicles attributing to the contributory negligence.
The petitioners claim that, Petitioner No.1 is the wife, petitioner No.2 is the minor daughter and petitioners No.3 is the mother of the deceased.
To prove the same, petitioner No.1 filed affidavit in lieu of her chief-examination and deposed about the above relationship.
The Aadhar cards of deceased and petitioners No.1 to 3 and contents of the police papers do fortify the said fact.
It is pertinent to note that, the relationship of the petitioners with the deceased has not been disputed by the respondents.

Since the evidence led by the petitioners is satisfactory and also taking into consideration the fact that there are no rival claimants, this Tribunal hold that the petitioners No.1 to 3 are the legal representative and legal heirs of the deceased M. Nagendra and they are entitled for compensation.
22. The petitioners have contended that the deceased was working as driver cum owner of TATA Intra Goods Tempo and earning Rs.50,000/- per month.
In order to prove the same, petitioners have not produced any documents before the court.
Therefore, considering the occupation of the deceased and year of the accident, I deem it just and reasonable to take the notional income of the deceased at Rs.16,000/- per month.
23. It is stated that the deceased was aged 30 years at the time of the accident.
The petitioners have produced adhaar card of the deceased at Ex.P9 which shows the year of birth of the deceased as 1993.
The accident occurred on 04.04.2023.
Hence, the age of the deceased at the time of accident is considered as 30 years.

The proper multiplier applicable to the case on hand is '17'.
24.

As per the decision of Hon'ble Apex Court reported in 2017 ACJ 2700 (SC) (National Insurance Company Limited Vs Pranay Sethi and others), if the person died in the motor accident, the income with respect to the future prospect has to taken into consideration while awarding compensation.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The Hon'ble Apex Court has provided the chart for age of the deceased and percentage for future prospects in between below the age of 40 years 40%, 40 years to 50 years 25% and 50 to 60 years 10%.
Nandini.

7 The deceased is not a permanent Employee and not a fixed salary person and he died at the age of 30 years.
Therefore, in this case, 40% income has to be taken into consideration for future prospects.

If 40% is added to the income of the deceased, then it comes to Rs.22,400/- p.m.
(Rs.16,000/- + 6,400/- i.e. 40%).
The deceased died leaving behind 3 dependents.

As per principle laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Sarala Verma Case, 1/3rd of his income is required to be deducted towards his personal expenses which comes to Rs.14,934/- p.m.(Rs.22,400 - Rs.7,466 = Rs.14,934/-).
25.
The income of the deceased is taken as Rs.14,934/- p.m. and the multiplier '17' is applied, then the loss of dependency comes to Rs.30,46,536/- (Rs.14,934 X 12 X 17).

Considering the above facts,
this Tribunal deems it just and reasonable to grant for compensation of Rs.30,46,536/- under the head of loss of dependency.

26. Further, as Law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi and others, the compensation towards loss to estate, funeral expenses and consortium is to be awarded.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The petitioners contended that they have spent substantial amount towards transportation of dead body, funeral and obsequies etc., but no documents are produced.

Hence this Tribunal award Rs.16,500/- towards loss to estate and Rs.16,500/- towards funeral expenses as enhanced at the rate of 10% on every 3 years and Rs.44,000/- towards consortium to the petitioner No.1.
27.
In this case, the petitioner No.2 is the minor daughter and petitioners No.3 is mother of the deceased

and as per the decision reported in (2018) 12 SCC 130 in the case of Magma General Insurance Company Limited V/s Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram and others, the petitioners No.2 and 3 are entitled for filial consortium, as the filial consortium is the right of the parents and children to get compensation in the case of an accidental death of a children and father as the case may be.

entities.text: Magma General Insurance Company Limited V/s Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: An accident leading to the death of father/son causes great shock and agony to the children and parents of the deceased and they lost their love and affection towards their father/son.
Therefore, petitioner No.2 and 3 are entitled for Rs.88,000/-(Rs.44,000 x 2) under the head of Filial consortium.

28. In total, the petitioners are entitled for the compensation under the following heads:

2. Towards loss of Consortium to the 44,000/-
petitioner No.1

3. Towards loss to estate 16,500/-
4. Towards transportation of dead 16,500/-

In all, the petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs.25,69,229/-.
29.

As regard the apportionment of compensation is concerned, it is not in dispute that the 1st petitioner is the widow and petitioners No.2 is the minor daughter and petitioners No.3 is the mother of the deceased.

Hence out of the total compensation, the petitioners No. 1 to 3 are entitled for compensation at the ratio of 50:30:20.
30.
The petitioners are claiming interest on the compensation amount.

Our Hon'ble High Court in the case rendered in Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others Vs Ulrich Belchior Fernandes and another (MFA.No.100090/2014 C/W MFA.No.25107/2013 dated 07.03.2018), has held that in the absence of any other law relating to interest on judgments, the MACT has to follow the provisions of Sec.34 of C.P.C and awarded interest @ 6% per annum.

sentences.text: Considering the aforesaid decision, I deem it proper to award interest at 6% per annum on the above compensation amount.
31.Liability:

Regarding fixation of liability is concerned, I have already observed that the accident was taken place due to the contributory negligence on the part of the driver of offending Lorry bearing Reg. No.TN-52-J-2262 and also the deceased.
It is not in dispute that 1st respondent is the owner of the offending vehicle.
The respondents have not proved the breach of any of the policy conditions.

As already discussed deceased/driver of Tata Intra goods tempo and the driver of Lorry bearing Reg. No.TN-52-J-2262 have contributed for happening of accident towards contributory negligence @ 20:80%.
Further the 20% contributory negligence of deceased is already deducted from the total compensation amount.
Hence, 1st respondent being the owner and 2 nd respondent being the insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation of its liability of 80%.
The 2 nd respondent shall indemnify the 1st respondent in payment of compensation amount.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 Partly in the Affirmative.
32. Issue No.3:

In view of my findings on issues No.1 and 2, I pass the following:
ORDER
The petition is allowed in part with cost.

The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.25,69,229/-(Rupees Twenty five lakhs sixty nine thousand two hundred and twenty nine only) with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.

9
The respondent No.2 is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of one month from the date of award.

On deposit of the award amount together with interest, the claimants are entitled for the compensation amount by way of apportionment as follows :
Petitioner No.1 - 50% Petitioner No.2 - 30% Petitioner No.3 - 20%

Further it is ordered that, 40% of the amount fallen to the share of the petitioners No.1 and 3 is ordered to be deposited in any nationalized bank for a period of 2 years in their respective names and remaining 60% of the amount is ordered to be released in their favour through E-payment on proper identification and verification.
However the said petitioners are at liberty to withdraw the periodical interest accrued on the deposit amount from time to time.

The share amount apportioned in the name of minor petitioner No.2 is ordered to be deposited in his name vide Fixed Deposit till he attains the age of majority, at any Nationalized/Scheduled Bank as per the choice of the next friend/Natural guardian of the said minor petitioner with liberty to the petitioner No.1 to draw periodical interest.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.

As per final order  For the following:
 REASONS 10. ISSUE NO.1 : It is the case of the petitioners that, on 04.04.2023 at 12.50 p.m. when the deceased was proceeding in his TATA Intra Goods Tempo bearing Reg. No.AP-39-UL-9821, near Sri Lakshmi Prasanna Nursery Garden, near Panthanahalli Village, on Kuppam-V.Kota Road, K.G.F.
Taluk, Kolar District, at that time, the driver of the Lorry bearing Reg. No.TN-52-J-2262 came from opposite direction i.e., from V. Kota side with high speed and in a rash and negligent manner.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The factum of negligence has to be proved like any other fact in issue.
Before dwelling into analyzing the factum of alleged negligence, it is relevant to have the conceptual aspects pertaining to factum of negligence.
There are four basic elements that a person has to fulfill in order to do a negligent act.
Duty: For committing a negligent act, there must be some duty on the part of the defendant.
After fulfilling the first criteria the plaintiff must prove that the defendant has breached the legal duty imposed on him/her.
The action of causing something: It means that the damage caused to the plaintiff is due to the act of the defendant.
Damages: At last what matters is, there must be some damage/injury that is caused to the plaintiff and this damages should be the direct consequence of the defendant's act.
Negligence means a breach of duty caused by omission to do something which has reasonable man guide by those consideration which ordinarily regulated conduct of human affairs would do which a prudent man would not do.
In common prevalence negligence connoted to the want of proper care and the rashness conveys the idea of recklessness or the doing of an act without due consideration.
One Sri Srinivasalu M. has put the law into motion by filing first information and accordingly, Ex.P.1 FIR is registered against the driver of offending vehicle for the offence punishable U/s. 279 and 304(A) of IPC and Sec 134(a and b) of MV Act.
The Charge sheet produced by the petitioners at Ex.P8 clearly discloses that the charge sheet is filed against the driver of the offending vehicle Lorry for rash and negligent driving under IPC 1860 U/s. 279, 304(A) and under Sec 134(a and b) of MV Act.
I.O has mentioned in chargesheet as per FSL report along with PM report which is showing 47.06 mg./100 ml. consumption of alcohol is itself is sufficient to come to conclusion that the deceased was under the influence of alcohol at the time of accident and such being the fact, the consumption of the alcohol is to be considered relying upon the said reports as the drink and drive has become menace to our society due to which several lives are lost and such act of drink and drive by consuming the alcohol has to be considered seriously and hence considering the charge sheet filed by the I.O. showing the deceased was under the influence of alcohol for which some part of contributory negligence for happening of the accident by the deceased if considered will meet the ends of justice.
Since the evidence led by the petitioners is satisfactory and also taking into consideration the fact that there are no rival claimants, this Tribunal hold that the petitioners No.1 to 3 are the legal representative and legal heirs of the deceased M. Nagendra and they are entitled for compensation.
7 The deceased is not a permanent Employee and not a fixed salary person and he died at the age of 30 years.
and as per the decision reported in (2018) 12 SCC 130 in the case of Magma General Insurance Company Limited V/s Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram and others, the petitioners No.2 and 3 are entitled for filial consortium, as the filial consortium is the right of the parents and children to get compensation in the case of an accidental death of a children and father as the case may be.
An accident leading to the death of father/son causes great shock and agony to the children and parents of the deceased and they lost their love and affection towards their father/son.
Our Hon'ble High Court in the case rendered in Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others Vs Ulrich Belchior Fernandes and another (MFA.No.100090/2014 C/W MFA.No.25107/2013 dated 07.03.2018), has held that in the absence of any other law relating to interest on judgments, the MACT has to follow the provisions of Sec.34 of C.P.C and awarded interest @ 6% per annum.
opennyai_summary.arguments: I would like to rely upon the decision rendered by Hon'ble Madras High Court in C.Misc. Appeal No.1842/2006 in K.Shanmugam vs. V.Krishnamurthy & Another, wherein it is held that the involvement of claimant in the accident due to the fact that he was in drunken stage and also alcohol consumption impairs consciousness and vision which becomes impossible to judge accurately how far the objects are whether it is night or day it can reduce the visibility of an object to the point of being below the limit of discernibility and punishment should be at-least a deterrent for other such persons getting away with minor punishment and fine.
opennyai_summary.decision:
Considering the above facts,
this Tribunal deems it just and reasonable to grant for compensation of Rs.30,46,536/- under the head of loss of dependency.
Hence this Tribunal award Rs.16,500/- towards loss to estate and Rs.16,500/- towards funeral expenses as enhanced at the rate of 10% on every 3 years and Rs.44,000/- towards consortium to the petitioner No.1.
27.
Therefore, petitioner No.2 and 3 are entitled for Rs.88,000/-(Rs.44,000 x 2) under the head of Filial consortium.
28. In total, the petitioners are entitled for the compensation under the following heads:
 Compensation heads Compensation  amount  1. Towards loss of dependency 30,46,536/-
2. Towards loss of Consortium to the 44,000/-
petitioner No.1
Towards loss of Filial consortium to 88,000/-
 petitioner No.2 and 3(Rs.44,000 x 2)
 Total Rs.32,11,536/-
 Less: 20% Contributory Negligence of Rs.6,42,307/-
 deceased  Compensation to be payable by the Rs.25,69,229/-
 respondent No.2
In all, the petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs.25,69,229/-.
29.
Hence out of the total compensation, the petitioners No. 1 to 3 are entitled for compensation at the ratio of 50:30:20.
30.
Considering the aforesaid decision, I deem it proper to award interest at 6% per annum on the above compensation amount.
Further the 20% contributory negligence of deceased is already deducted from the total compensation amount.
Hence, 1st respondent being the owner and 2 nd respondent being the insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation of its liability of 80%.
The 2 nd respondent shall indemnify the 1st respondent in payment of compensation amount.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 Partly in the Affirmative.
32. Issue No.3:
In view of my findings on issues No.1 and 2, I pass the following:
ORDER
The petition is allowed in part with cost.
The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.25,69,229/-(Rupees Twenty five lakhs sixty nine thousand two hundred and twenty nine only) with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
Nandini.M vs Sellappa Gounder.P on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/108054948/
9
The respondent No.2 is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of one month from the date of award.
On deposit of the award amount together with interest, the claimants are entitled for the compensation amount by way of apportionment as follows :
Petitioner No.1 - 50% Petitioner No.2 - 30% Petitioner No.3 - 20%
Further it is ordered that, 40% of the amount fallen to the share of the petitioners No.1 and 3 is ordered to be deposited in any nationalized bank for a period of 2 years in their respective names and remaining 60% of the amount is ordered to be released in their favour through E-payment on proper identification and verification.
However the said petitioners are at liberty to withdraw the periodical interest accrued on the deposit amount from time to time.
The share amount apportioned in the name of minor petitioner No.2 is ordered to be deposited in his name vide Fixed Deposit till he attains the age of majority, at any Nationalized/Scheduled Bank as per the choice of the next friend/Natural guardian of the said minor petitioner with liberty to the petitioner No.1 to draw periodical interest.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
